children: Hero Motors and Jindal Supreme shares hit their upper circuit limits in Wednesday's trading session after making strong market debuts, while SS Retail extended its rise to around 65 percent from its issue price.
Hero Motors shares hit the 20 percent upper circuit limit to quote at Rs 98.40 per share on the NSE, extending its post-listing rise to 17.14 percent.
The rise came after the auto components maker made a muted market debut, listing over 2 percent lower against the issue price of Rs 84.
The stock started trading at Rs 82.10, a discount of 2.26 percent from the issue price on the BSE.
At the NSE, the stock made its debut at Rs 82, down 2.38 percent.
The Rs 1,000-crore IPO had a price band of Rs 79-84 per equity share.

Shivani Nyati, Head of Wealth at Swastika Investmart, said the company benefits from a strong position in powertrain solutions and the growth potential of electric vehicles. However, its valuation at around 69-74 times price-to-earnings remains significantly higher than the peer average of 50.2 times.
Although return on net worth has improved to 8.53 percent and EBITDA margin to around 10.2 percent, both remain below key peers, while high customer concentration adds another risk, she said.

"Given the strong business prospects but limited valuation cushion, our post-listing view is Neutral. Investors can wait for better valuation or price consolidation before considering fresh positions, while existing investors may consider holding with a stop-loss around Rs 75-77," Nyati said.

The company has been investing heavily in new joint ventures, including tie-ups for CVT, hub-motor EDUs and dual-clutch transmissions, which should support growth ahead. Growth has been sluggish recently and margins remain modest, said Sarvam Goel, Founder of Pocketful.
"Investors who received allotment should hold and track management commentary. This is better suited to a medium to long-term view than a quick trade," he added.
Jindal Supreme (India) shares also hit the 5 percent upper circuit limit to trade at Rs 126 per share on the NSE, extending their post-listing rise to 35.48 percent.
Jindal Supreme manufactures steel pipes, tubes, crash barriers and GI tubular poles and is unrelated to the larger Jindal Group despite the similar name.

"Growth has been largely flat between FY23 and FY26, with the recent improvement in profitability driven mainly by better steel price realisations rather than volume growth, and margins jumped noticeably just ahead of the IPO," Goel said.
"Coming at about 21x FY26 earnings, we don't see much valuation upside from here. Treat this as a listing gain trade rather than a hold," he added.
Shares of Jindal Supreme (India) Ltd listed 31 percent higher than the issue price of Rs 93. The stock made its debut at Rs 121.90, up 31 percent from the issue price on the BSE.
At the NSE, it started trading at Rs 120, a premium of 29 percent.
Dr Ravi Singh, Chief Research Officer at Master Capital Services, said domestic demand for steel pipes is projected to grow at a CAGR of approximately 5.5 percent between fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2030.

"In the short term, investors may focus on the company's revenue growth, order execution and ability to maintain profitability amid business expansion, while long-term investors may track capacity expansion, order-book growth and its presence in the steel and related products market," Singh said.
"Upcoming results could provide further visibility on capacity utilisation, margin stability and cash-flow generation," he added.
Meanwhile, SS Retail shares extended their post-listing rise to 69.04 percent.
Shares of SS Retail made a strong debut, listing at a premium of nearly 51 percent against the issue price of Rs 424.
The stock listed at Rs 639.10, up 50.73 percent from the issue price on the BSE.
At the NSE, the stock made its debut at Rs 624, registering a jump of 47.16 percent.

SS Retail is a multi-brand mobile phone retail chain with about 500 stores across more than 200 cities, though nearly 90 per cent of its stores and revenue still come from Maharashtra, with expansion into new states now underway.
The business also offers accessories and mobile exchange services. The anchor book was strong, and the overall issue was subscribed 107 times.
However, the pricing is rich, at over 50 times FY26 earnings.
"This works better as a listing gain trade than a long-term hold, so investors can book profits on debut," Goel said.
